title: Study on Patients' Assessment of the Quality of Care During Their Treatment for Cholecystectomies at Limoges University Hospital
official: A Prospective Observational Study on Patients' Assessment of the Quality of Care During Their Treatment for Cholecystectomies at Limoges University Hospital
summary:
SATISCHOL is a prospective, monocentric observational study designed to assess pain management and quality of care in patients undergoing elective cholecystectomy at Limoges University Hospital, France.

The primary objective is to assess the proportion of patients reporting a visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score below 4 two hours after surgery, in association with the occurrence of no postoperative complication or a grade I early postoperative complication according to the Clavien-Dindo classification, within four weeks after surgery.

Secondary objectives include assessing early postoperative pain, describing postoperative complications and intraoperative pain management techniques, and evaluating changes in patients' quality of life using the Gastrointestinal Quality of Life Index (GIQLI) and EQ-5D-5L questionnaires. Patient-reported experience will also be assessed using a study-specific questionnaire (PREMS).

A total of 70 participants are expected to be enrolled. Patients will be followed for approximately 3 to 6 weeks after surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Patients undergoing elective cholecystectomy.
* Patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery or minimally invasive surgery, including conversion to open laparotomy when necessary.
* Patients able to complete questionnaires independently or with the assistance of a caregiver.
* Patients covered by a health insurance scheme.
* Patients who have not objected to participation in the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients undergoing emergency surgery.
* Patients undergoing cholecystectomy when gallbladder removal is not the primary purpose of the surgical procedure.
* Patients with a history of chronic gastrointestinal disease.
* Patients with known gallbladder cancer.
* Patients scheduled for open laparotomy.
